title: Wiring the base
say: LittleBot, version five. Wiring the base, step by step. This covers the batteries, the motor driver, the motors' encoders, the three servos, and the small R P twenty forty board that runs them.

title: Batteries out, switch off
cap: No batteries in the drawer, drive switch OFF, until the end
Jumper wires: male-male and male-female
Small screwdriver, wire stripper, multimeter
say: Keep the batteries out of the drawer, and the drive switch off, until near the end. You'll need jumper wires, both male to male, and male to female. A small screwdriver, a wire stripper, and a multimeter.

title: Load the program first, on your computer
cap: Do it now, while the board is easy to reach
No Wi-Fi: the Pi talks to it through 3 wires
say: Part one. Load the R P twenty forty's program on your computer now, while the board is easy to reach. It has no Wi-Fi, and doesn't need any. The Pi talks to it through three wires.

title: Plug it in holding BOOT
cap: Install Thonny (thonny.org)
Hold BOOT, plug in the USB-C cable, let go
A drive called RPI-RP2 appears
say: Install Thonny, from thonny dot org. Hold the board's boot button, plug it into the computer with a USB C cable, then let go. A drive called R P I, dash, R P 2 appears. A brand new board may show it without the button.

title: Install MicroPython
cap: Thonny: click the bottom-right corner → Install MicroPython…
Variant: Raspberry Pi · Pico / Pico H → Install
The drive goes away when it's done: that's normal
say: In Thonny, click the bottom right corner of the window, and choose Install MicroPython. Pick the Raspberry Pi Pico variant, and click Install. When it's done, the drive goes away. That's normal.

title: Save main.py on the board
cap: Open main.py (the file I sent)
File → Save as… → Raspberry Pi Pico
Name: main.py
say: Open main dot pie, the file I sent you. Choose File, Save as, then Raspberry Pi Pico, and save it on the board with the name main dot pie.

title: Test it
cap: Click Stop, then type PING → PONG littlebot-base 1
Type B → B null (nothing connected yet: right)
Unplug the board
say: Click Stop. Then type the word ping in Thonny's shell, and press Enter. The board answers: pong, littlebot base. Type B, and it says B null, because nothing is connected yet. That's right. Unplug the board.

title: The board onto the breadboard
cap: USB-C end at row 1, across the middle gap
Each pin has its own row, with 2 free holes beside it
Every wire goes into one of those free holes
say: Part two, the breadboard. Press the R P twenty forty in, with its USB C end at row one, across the middle gap. Each pin gets its own row, with two free holes beside it. Every wire in this video goes into one of those free holes.

title: Check the labels on your board
cap: GP0: top-left pin, beside the USB-C
VSYS: 2nd pin on the right
Different? Stop and send me a photo
say: Check the labels printed on your board. G P zero must be the top left pin, beside the USB connector, and V sys the second pin on the right. If yours are different, stop, and send me a photo.

title: Where everything sits
cap: On the deck: breadboard (robot's left), 4 Wagos (middle)
Motor driver (back right), 5 V converter (front right)
Pi + UPS behind the deck, batteries in the front drawer
say: Here's where everything sits on the deck. The breadboard on the robot's left, the four Wago connectors in the middle, the motor driver at the back right, and the five volt converter in front of it. The Pi stands behind the deck, and the batteries slide into the drawer at the front.

title: Everything we'll connect, laid flat
cap: Pi's pins · motors · motor driver · breadboard
4 Wagos · batteries, fuse, switch · converter · 3 servos
say: And here's everything we'll connect, laid out flat. The Pi's pins at the top left. The motors on the left, already joined to the motor driver below them. The breadboard in the middle. Then the four Wagos, the batteries, fuse and switch, the converter, and the three servos.

title: How a Wago works
cap: Strip 11 mm
Lift the lever, push the wire in all the way, close it
Tug it: it must not come out
say: Part three, power. First, how a Wago works. Strip eleven millimetres of insulation. Lift the orange lever, push the wire in all the way, and close the lever. Then tug the wire. It must not come out.

title: The batteries connect with a plug
cap: An XT30 plug pair (with wires): it only fits one way
Holder's red + black → the female half: solder, heat-shrink
The male half stays in the robot, in the drawer's bay
say: The batteries aren't wired in for good. They connect through a two pin plug, so the drawer can go in last, and come all the way out. Get an X T thirty plug pair, with wires. Solder the female half to the battery holder's two wires: red to red, black to black, and cover each joint with heat shrink. The male half stays in the robot, in the drawer's bay.

title: The robot's half: + through the fuse and switch
cap: Male half's red → 5 A fuse → a switch tab
The switch's other tab → Wago A slot 1
Solder + heat-shrink, or crimp spade connectors on the tabs
say: The male half's red wire goes through the five amp fuse, to one tab of the drive switch. The switch's other tab goes to Wago A, slot one. Solder these joints, and cover them with heat shrink, or crimp spade connectors onto the switch's tabs.

title: Which two tabs?
cap: Meter on beep (continuity)
Find the 2 tabs that beep with the switch ON, not OFF
The 3rd tab only lights the switch: leave it empty
say: Which tabs? The switch has three. Set your meter to beep, and find the two tabs that beep when the switch is on, and stay silent when it's off. Use those two. The third tab only lights the switch. Leave it empty.

title: The robot's half: − to Wago B
cap: Male half's black → Wago B slot 1
Both its wires go down through the hole at the deck's front:
the plug hangs in the drawer's bay, waiting for the batteries
say: The male half's black wire goes to Wago B, slot one. Both of its wires run down through the hole at the front of the deck, so the plug hangs in the drawer's bay, waiting for the batteries.

title: The motor driver's green block
cap: Loosen its 2 screws
Wago A slot 2 → +      Wago B slot 2 → −
Push the bare ends in, tighten
say: Now the motor driver's green power block. Loosen its two screws. Wago A, slot two, goes to the plus side, and Wago B, slot two, to the minus side. Push each bare end in, and tighten.

title: The 5 V converter: input
cap: Check the IN and OUT labels on yours
IN + → Wago A slot 3      IN − → Wago B slot 3
say: The converter turns the batteries into five volts, for the servos and the R P twenty forty. Check the labels on yours. Its input: plus to Wago A, slot three. Minus to Wago B, slot three.

title: The 5 V converter: output
cap: OUT + → Wago C slot 1      OUT − → Wago D slot 1
If the output ends in a plug: cut it off, strip the 2 wires
say: Its output: plus to Wago C, slot one. Minus to Wago D, slot one. If its output ends in a plug, cut the plug off, and strip the two wires.

title: Link the two grounds
cap: A short wire: Wago B slot 5 → Wago D slot 5
say: Then link the two ground Wagos, with a short wire from Wago B, slot five, to Wago D, slot five.

title: Check for shorts (no batteries)
cap: Switch OFF, meter on beep
A to B: no beep.  C to D: no beep
A chirp that stops at once is the capacitors: fine
say: Now check for shorts, before any batteries. Switch off, and set the meter to beep. Touch Wago A and Wago B: it must not beep. Then Wago C and Wago D: no beep. A short chirp that stops at once is just the capacitors charging. That's fine.

title: A quick live test
cap: Cells in the holder, plug it in, switch ON
A to B: 7 to 9.5 V      C to D: 5 V
Then switch OFF and unplug the batteries again
say: A quick live test. Put the cells in the holder, plug it in, and switch on. Red probe on Wago A, black on Wago B: seven to nine and a half volts. Red on Wago C, black on Wago D: five volts. If either is wrong, switch off and check. Then switch off, and unplug the batteries again.

title: Its power
cap: VSYS (row 2, right) → Wago C slot 5
GND (row 3, right) → Wago B slot 4
For a Wago end: cut a jumper, strip the cut end 11 mm
say: Part four, the R P twenty forty's wires. First its power. From V sys, row two on the right, to Wago C, slot five. From the ground pin, row three on the right, to Wago B, slot four. For each Wago end, cut a jumper wire, and strip the cut end.

title: The motor driver's control pins
cap: GP10 → M1A   GP11 → M1B   GP12 → M2A   GP13 → M2B
GND (row 18, left) → the driver's GND
Leave the driver's 5V pin empty · follow the labels on it
say: The motor driver's control pins. G P ten, to M one A. G P eleven, to M one B. G P twelve, to M two A. G P thirteen, to M two B. And the ground pin in row eighteen, to the driver's G N D. Leave the driver's five volt pin empty.

title: Left motor's encoder
cap: 4 thin wires besides the red and white
yellow → GP6    green → GP7
black → GND (row 8, left)
say: The motors' encoders. Each motor has four thin wires, besides its red and white. Left motor: yellow, to G P six. Green, to G P seven. Black, to the ground pin in row eight.

title: Right motor's encoder
cap: yellow → GP8    green → GP9
black → GND (row 13, left)
say: Right motor: yellow, to G P eight. Green, to G P nine. Black, to the ground pin in row thirteen.

title: Both blue wires: 3.3 V
cap: Both blues → 3V3 OUT (row 5, right)
Never 5 V: the RP2040's pins take 3.3 V only
say: Both blue wires go to three point three volts, row five on the right. Never five volts. The R P twenty forty's pins only take three point three.

title: Three wires each
cap: brown = ground   red = 5 V   orange = signal
Their plugs don't fit a Wago:
make a 'tail' of 3 jumpers for each servo
say: Part five, the servos. Each servo has three wires. Brown is ground, red is power, and orange is the signal. The servos' plugs don't fit the Wagos, so for each servo, make a tail of three jumpers.

title: Head servo's tail
cap: orange → GP14 (row 19, left)
red → Wago C slot 2    brown → Wago D slot 2
Label it: HEAD
say: Head servo. Orange, to G P fourteen. Red, to Wago C, slot two. Brown, to Wago D, slot two. Put a tape label on the tail: head.

title: Left arm servo's tail
cap: orange → GP15 (row 20, left)
red → Wago C slot 3    brown → Wago D slot 3
say: Left arm servo. Orange, to G P fifteen. Red, to Wago C, slot three. Brown, to Wago D, slot three.

title: Right arm servo's tail
cap: orange → GP16 (row 20, right)
red → Wago C slot 4    brown → Wago D slot 4
say: Right arm servo. Orange, to G P sixteen, row twenty on the right. Red, to Wago C, slot four. Brown, to Wago D, slot four.

title: Plugging a servo onto its tail
cap: When the body and head go on:
each jumper's pin into the matching hole of the servo's plug
brown to brown · red to red · orange to orange
say: Later, when the body and the head go on, push each jumper's pin into the matching hole of that servo's plug. Brown to brown, red to red, and orange to orange. A servo plugged in backwards won't move.

title: Tip: centre a servo at the bench
cap: Board on USB, servo: brown → GND, red → VBUS, orange → GP14
Thonny: type CENTER
One servo at a time, nothing on its horn
say: A tip. To centre a servo at the bench, before you fit the pinion or an arm, use the computer. With the board on USB, connect the servo's brown to a ground pin, red to V bus, the top right pin, and orange to G P fourteen. In Thonny, type the word center. One servo at a time, with nothing on its horn.

title: Two resistors
cap: 22 kΩ: GP26 (row 10, right) → row 22
10 kΩ: row 10 → AGND (row 8, right)
say: Part six, the battery sense. Two resistors let the R P twenty forty measure the batteries. A twenty two k resistor, from G P twenty six, row ten on the right, down to row twenty two. And a ten k resistor, from row ten, to the analog ground pin in row eight.

title: Battery + to row 22
cap: Wago A slot 4 → row 22 (right)
8.5 V becomes 2.7 V on GP26: safe for the pin
say: Then a wire from Wago A, slot four, to row twenty two. The resistors turn the batteries' eight and a half volts into under three volts, which the pin can safely read.

title: The Pi's pins
cap: The 40-pin header, along the Pi's bottom edge
Outer row, from the end away from the USB ports:
pins 2, 4 = 5 V (never!)   6 = GND   8 = TX   10 = RX
say: Part seven, the link to the Pi. Its forty pin header runs along its bottom edge. On the outer row, counting from the end away from the USB ports: pins two and four are five volts. Never touch them. Pin six is ground, pin eight is T X, and pin ten is R X.

title: Three wires to the Pi
cap: Male-female jumpers
GP0 → pin 10    GP1 → pin 8 (they cross: TX to RX)
GND (row 3, left) → pin 6
say: Use male to female jumpers. G P zero goes to pin ten. G P one goes to pin eight. They cross over: what one board sends, the other receives. And the ground in row three goes to pin six.

title: Turn on the Pi's serial port
say: On the Pi, turn the port on. Add the line, D T param equals uart zero equals on, at the end of the file, slash boot, slash firmware, slash config dot T X T. Then reboot. And get LittleBot's latest code onto the Pi.

title: Batteries in, the drawer last
cap: Cells into the holder, the holder into the drawer
Plug it into the plug hanging in the bay
Slide the drawer in: the plug folds in above the holder · 2 screws
say: Part eight, the first power up. Put the six cells in the holder, and the holder in the drawer. Plug it into the plug hanging in the bay. Then slide the drawer in. The plug and its wires fold into the space above the holder. Fit the door's two screws. To change the batteries later: switch off, take out the two screws, slide the drawer out, and unplug it.

title: Switch on
cap: Robot on a box: wheels off the table
Switch ON
The switch, the driver and the RP2040 light up
say: Stand the robot on a box, with its wheels off the table, and switch on. The switch lights up, and so do the power lights on the motor driver and the R P twenty forty.

title: Is it talking?
say: On the Pi, in the LittleBot folder, run: python three, scripts, slash, base test dot pie, ping. It answers pong. Then run it with battery. It shows the batteries' voltage.

title: Centre the servos
term: OK - the 3 servos are at 90 degrees and stay there
say: Run it with center. All three servos go to ninety degrees, and stay there. That's the position to fit the pinion and the arms in.

title: Set the wheels' directions
term: Spinning the left wheel slowly for 2 seconds...
Did the left wheel turn the way it turns when the
the left encoder counts up going forwards: good
say: Run it with wheels. Each wheel spins slowly for two seconds, and it asks you which way it turned. It sets the directions for you, and saves them on the board.

title: Calibrate the encoders
term: Mark the left wheel (a bit of tape), then press Enter
Turn the left wheel FORWARDS exactly 5 whole turns...
say: Last, run it with calibrate. Mark each wheel with tape, turn it forwards exactly five times by hand, and press Enter. It works out the encoder's counts per turn, and saves them.

title: The base is wired
cap: Something doesn't answer? Check that wire's two ends
Unsure? Send me a photo
say: That's it. The base is wired. If something doesn't answer, check that wire's two ends against this video. And if you're unsure about anything, send me a photo.
